de24_reid.topic: Re-identification of 'anonymous' data: studies and documented cases

claims.text: Sweeney (2000) estimated 87% (216m of 248m) of the US population likely unique on 5-digit ZIP, gender and date of birth, using 1990 Census data; county+gender+DOB 18%; she bought the Cambridge, Mass. voter list for $20
Golle recomputed on 2000 Census: 63% uniquely identified by gender, ZIP, full DOB; 'generally agree' with Sweeney but fewer
Sweeney in 1997 identified Massachusetts Governor Bill Weld's medical records using publicly accessible records
de Montjoye et al. 2013: 15 months of mobility data for 1.5 million people; four spatio-temporal points uniquely identify 95%; uniqueness decays only as ~1/10 power of resolution
de Montjoye et al. 2015 (Science): 3 months of credit-card records for 1.1 million people; four spatiotemporal points reidentify 90%; price raises risk 22% on average; women more reidentifiable
Rocher, Hendrickx, de Montjoye 2019: 99.98% of Americans would be correctly re-identified in any dataset using 15 demographic attributes

Narayanan and Shmatikov: Netflix Prize data on ~500,000 subscribers; with 8 ratings (2 may be wrong) and dates within 14 days, 99% of records uniquely identified; 2 ratings with dates within 3 days suffice for 68%; IMDb cross-match revealed apparent political preferences

NYT Dec 2018: at least 75 companies receive anonymous, precise location data from apps; several claim up to 200 million US devices; locations as often as every two seconds; teacher Lisa Magrin identified; industry says data tied to unique ID not name

NYT Opinion 19 Dec 2019: one file of more than 50 billion pings from 12 million+ phones, 2016-17, Washington/NY/SF/LA; traced a senior DoD official and others; 'child's play to connect real names to the dots'; Paul Ohm: precise longitudinal geolocation 'absolutely impossible to anonymize'

The Pillar bought 'commercially available' location data from an unnamed vendor (2018-2020) and matched it to Msgr Jeffrey Burrill's phone and Grindr use; he resigned July 2021; Grindr called it a 'witch hunt' and said it did not believe it was the source

FTC Office of Technology (July 2024): 'hashes aren't anonymous'; a hash 'still creates a unique signature that can track a person or device over time'; data is anonymous only when it 'can never be associated back to a person'; cases Nomi 2015, BetterHelp, Premom 2023, InMarket 2024

de24_fusion.topic: Brokers, fusion centres, ALPR, government data reuse, HART

claims.text: Flock paused pilots with CBP and HSI on 25 Aug 2025 after Illinois SoS audit found CBP accessed Illinois plate data in violation of state law; cameras in 4,000+ communities; Langley: 'We clearly communicated poorly'; federal searches now labelled and limited to one-to-one

Woodburn, Oregon audit: DHS and Border Patrol ran 6,089 searches Jan-Nov 2025 via a Flock trial allowing broad multi-network searches; city ended contract end of April 2026; cameras removed by 13 May; police policy bars immigration use
ALPR errors: Brittney Gilliam family held at gunpoint, Aurora CO, Aug 2020, $1.9m settlement; Denise Green SF 2009 '3' read as '7', $495,000; one study: state misread on 1 in 10 plates

LexisNexis contract 70CMSD21C00000001 (Feb 2021, ~$24.51m) gave ICE Accurint/LexID; jail-booking data added 2021; ends 31 Aug 2026; 10 Aug 2026 notice of $6.7m sole-source bridge; work statement requires APIs to 'the Palantir platform', PenLink, ICE Data Analytics; >1.2m Accurint person searches Mar-Sep 2021 (Just Futures Law)

Thomson Reuters CLEAR renewed sole-source for DHS from 31 Mar 2026 ('only CLEAR provides the range of law enforcement data'); data listed include utility data, credit bureaus, LPR; LEIDS-5 $22.8m May 2021-May 2026; TR: 'Palantir is not a customer of CLEAR'; 'We do not comment on specific customer contracts'

NCTUE utility header data (names, addresses, SSNs of 170m+ people) licensed to Equifax and sold into CLEAR, used by ICE; revealed Feb 2021; NCTUE told Equifax to stop Oct 2021; Equifax stopped law-enforcement provision 23 Oct 2021 after Wyden pressure

Senate PSI bipartisan report (2 Oct 2012): DHS fusion-centre intelligence 'oftentimes shoddy, rarely timely'; no unique contribution to disrupting a terror plot shown; DHS spending estimates $289m-$1.4bn since 2003; >70 fusion centres; spending on SUVs, TVs, cell-phone tracking devices
Report said fusion centre intelligence was 'sometimes endangering citizens' civil liberties and Privacy Act protections'; 72 centres

SAVE: in May 2025 USCIS linked SSA data; 15 Aug 2025 last-four SSN lookups; free and bulk; 33m+ voters run by Sept 2025; under 1% needed manual review; queries kept 10 years; agreements allow DHS use 'for any purpose permitted by law'; USCIS has not published accuracy testing

GAO-23-105959 (12 Sep 2023): HART meant to replace legacy biometric system holding 290m+ identities; IOC slipped from 31 Dec 2020 to 30 Sep 2023 and further rebaseline needed; costs +$354m; 5 of 12 OMB privacy requirements met; 9 recommendations all open
Northrop Grumman won $95m contract (announced 27 Feb 2018) for first two increments of HART, using face, fingerprint and iris

Biometric Update 31 Aug 2026: Kyle Schutt, who moved through agencies with DOGE, became acting DHS CIO and OBIM director; HART 'scheduled to reach initial operational capability no later than September 2026'
ODNI report on commercially available information (dated Jan 2022, declassified 12 Jun 2023): CAI 'can reveal sensitive and intimate information about individuals'; IC acquires 'significant amount'

California DROP: one deletion request to all registered brokers from 1 Jan 2026; brokers process from 1 Aug 2026 every 45 days; more than 500 registered brokers; broker defined as business selling data a consumer didn't give it directly

Judge Chhabria (29 Dec 2025, effective 6 Jan 2026): for 20 plaintiff states, HHS may share with ICE only Medicaid data on people unlawfully present and only status, address, phone, DOB, Medicaid ID; health records barred

ICE contract (reported 27 Jan 2018) with West Publishing (Thomson Reuters) in partnership with Vigilant Solutions for access to billions of plate records; ICE: data is 'one tool in support of its investigations'; ICE had cancelled a similar 2014 request over privacy concerns and did a privacy impact assessment

In February 2014 DHS Secretary Jeh Johnson ordered cancellation of an ICE solicitation for access to a nationwide licence-plate tracking database, saying it was posted without ICE leadership's awareness, and ordered a review
